description:
Two smaller robustness/consistency issues in the throughput executor.

1. TIMED-OUT STREAM LEAK: StreamRunner.execute enforces per-stream timeout via
   `future.result(timeout=...)` but cannot cancel a running thread
   (benchbox/core/throughput/runner.py:87-113). A timed-out stream keeps
   executing in the background, still holding its connection and consuming
   CPU/server resources, while the executor records it as failed and moves on.
   During a long throughput run this means the reported TTT window can overlap
   zombie streams that are still hammering the DB -- skewing both the failed
   run's accounting and any subsequent phase (e.g. maintenance) that starts
   while zombies run. At minimum this should be surfaced; ideally streams
   should be cooperatively cancellable or isolated so a timeout actually stops
   work.

2. DIVERGENT SUCCESS GATES: TPC-H throughput uses a configurable
   min_success_rate (default 0.99) (benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py:38,
   135-137) while TPC-DS hardcodes 0.70
   (benchbox/core/tpcds/throughput_test.py:186, and again per-stream at :393).
   The divergence is documented as intentional
   (benchbox/core/throughput/runner.py:11-15 and
   docs/development/throughput-result-alignment.md) but 0.70 vs 0.99 is a large
   gap that changes whether a run is declared successful. Reconcile against the
   TPC-DS spec: make the TPC-DS gate configurable like TPC-H (keeping the
   spec-derived default) and document the spec citation for each threshold.

anti_patterns.instead: prefer cooperative cancel / process isolation / explicit surfacing.

preserves.behavior: Default TPC-H gate stays 0.99; default TPC-DS gate stays its current spec value unless the spec says otherwise.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py:TPCHThroughputTestConfig.min_success_rate — the configurable-gate pattern to mirror for TPC-DS.
benchbox/experimental/concurrency/executor.py — has a resource-monitor thread pattern usable to detect/report zombie streams.
docs/development/throughput-result-alignment.md — documents the current divergence; update alongside any change.

verifications.description: Timeout path annotates leaked streams; TPC-DS gate is configurable

work_units.notes:
Discovered the per-stream timeout was dead code: StreamRunner.execute()
called future.result(timeout=timeout) on a future already yielded by
as_completed() (which only yields done() futures), so TimeoutError could
never actually raise in real usage -- verified with a standalone repro
before changing anything. Fixed by passing timeout to
as_completed(pending, timeout=...) itself, with a fallback loop that
classifies any still-pending future as timed-out/leaked when that call
raises. streams_executed/streams_successful/errors accounting is
unchanged (shared via a small _record_completed_future helper used by
both the main loop and the fallback). A leaked stream now always logs
via logger.warning(...) (previously gated on config.verbose, so it could
be entirely silent) and result.errors gets an explicit message noting
Python cannot forcibly cancel the running thread.
work_units.summary: Surface timed-out (leaked) streams: annotate the result and log that background execution may continue

work_units.notes:
Added config.cancel_on_timeout (default False) on both
TPCHThroughputTestConfig and TPCDSThroughputTestConfig. When enabled,
StreamRunner.execute() creates one threading.Event per stream, exposed
via a runtime-only config._stream_cancel_events attribute (not a
declared config field, so unaffected configs/test doubles are
unaffected), and sets the timed-out stream's own event only (never
every stream's event -- one slow stream must not cancel healthy ones).
Each spec's _execute_stream query loop polls its own event once per
query and breaks early if set, marking the stream unsuccessful with an
explicit cancellation error message. Never hard-kills a thread. Even
with this enabled, exiting execute()'s ThreadPoolExecutor context still
blocks until every submitted thread returns (implicit
shutdown(wait=True)); cooperative cancellation shortens that wait to
roughly one more query's execution time instead of leaving it
unbounded.
work_units.summary: Add a cooperative-cancellation or isolation option so a stream timeout can actually stop work (opt-in)

work_units.notes:
Added TPCDSThroughputTestConfig.min_success_rate (default 0.70,
mirroring TPCHThroughputTestConfig.min_success_rate). Replaced all
THREE independently hard-coded 0.7 literals (run()'s overall gate,
_finalize_stream_success()'s per-stream gate, and
validate_results()'s gate -- the TODO's own description only names the
first two, but a third existed) with reads of this single field.
Checked both bundled spec PDFs (_sources/tpc-h/specification.pdf,
_sources/tpc-ds/specification/specification_4.0.0.pdf) directly for a
partial-success/acceptable-failure-rate clause: none exists in either
spec. TPC-H 5.1.1.6 defines a failed run as one that "did not complete
successfully due to unforeseen system failures" -- no tolerance
percentage. The prior TPC-H comment ("TPC-H spec allows up to 1% query
failures") was an invented citation (the spec's only 1%/0.99
occurrences are unrelated numeric result-value tolerances, Clause
2.2.4.2) and has been corrected. Both 0.99 and 0.70 are now documented
as BenchBox-internal usability tolerances, not official TPC compliance
gates, on each config dataclass and in
docs/development/throughput-result-alignment.md.
work_units.summary: Make the TPC-DS throughput success gate configurable (spec-default) and cite the spec threshold for both benchmarks
